course_name_original: Mantenimiento de Máquinas y Seguridad en el Trabajo

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and material resistance to the behavior of real solids

Maintenance management derived from equipment deterioration problems and their consequences for industrial activity reliability, equipment safety, and even personal safety. Economic repercussions. Application of different maintenance strategies or types, with in-depth study of each. Basic notions of occupational health and safety, including its implementation in companies and integration with the production system.

Students must acquire the ability to identify faults in different machines, implement an industrial maintenance system, and implement, modify, or develop safety systems so that equipment meets the minimum safety conditions established in R.D. 1215/97 and its subsequent updates.
Be able to detect deviations in work equipment regarding R.D. 1215/97.

syllabus_topics: Tema 1: Introduction. Types of maintenance. Historical evolution of maintenance. Predictive maintenance techniques. Failure theories. Failure distribution. Failure mechanisms. Maintenance parameters or indices: reliability, maintainability, availability. Examples.
Tema 5. Shaft Supports. Couplings and Shaft Alignment.
Tema 7. Maintenance of Industrial Buildings and Facilities.
Tema 8. Introduction to Occupational Risk Prevention.
Tema 9. Work and its safety: Spanish regulations. Regulations on Occupational Risk Prevention.
Tema 11. Risk assessment and prevention planning.
Tema 12. Minimum safety and health provisions in the workplace.
Tema 13. Safety in Machines and equipment.
teaching_methods: Participatory master classes for theory sessions (13 sessions)
Practical sessions in laboratory or computer room, based on conducting tests and analyzing results, performed in work groups (10 sessions)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is the weighted average of periodic deliverable assignments (50%) and an on-site written exam (50%). A minimum grade of 5 is required in each part to pass the subject. For the extraordinary call, evaluation includes a practical exam (50%) and an on-site written exam (50%). Students who passed the periodic assignments in the ordinary call will retain that grade and are exempt from the practical exam. A minimum grade of 5 is required in each part to pass. For unique evaluation, applicable under Article 8, assessment is a practical lab exam and an on-site written exam, both weighted 50%.
